newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Spring/White Wheat - Basis steady to firmer.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Spring/White Wheat - Basis steady to firmer.

text.p: Basis levels for dark northern spring were steady to firmer Tuesday across the northern U.S. grain belt, dealers reported.
Dealers said that although a fair amount of grain was moving into Minneapolis, basis bids actually rose there.
In the Pacific Northwest, however, basis bids remained mostly unchanged.

MGE March spring wheat rose six cents per bushel Tuesday on decent commercial pricing, traders said. But the basis for 14 percent protein spring wheat also rose five cents in Minneapolis, so the cash bid was up 11 cents.
"There were quite a few trainloads received (on the cash trading floor) but the market appears to be taking it all in and paying decent money for it," a Minneapolis grain dealer reported.

Meanwhile, another winter storm dropped several inches of snow across Montana and was due to bring more snow to the Dakotas. But dealers said temperatures were not expected to be as frigid as last week.
